reading: Every plus-shaped group of five 0 cells (a 0 cell whose four orthogonal neighbours are also 0) is painted 3; overlapping pluses merge.

new_rows.name: plus0
new_rows.datalog:
pc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C0), C0 = 0, Ya = Y - 1, px(Ya, X, C1), C1 = 0, Yb = Y + 1, px(Yb, X, C2), C2 = 0, Xa = X - 1, px(Y, Xa, C3), C3 = 0, Xb = X + 1, px(Y, Xb, C4), C4 = 0.
plus0(Y, X) :- pc(Y, X).
plus0(Y, X) :- pc(Y0, X), Y = Y0 - 1.
plus0(Y, X) :- pc(Y0, X), Y = Y0 + 1.
plus0(Y, X) :- pc(Y, X0), X = X0 - 1.
plus0(Y, X) :- pc(Y, X0), X = X0 + 1.

why: cells of 0-pluses become 3, all other cells unchanged (bg varies between 0 and 8, so colour 0 is literal)

reading: From the single marker a colour-1 line runs up and down the marker's column to both edges (marker kept); at the top edge it turns along the top row to one side, at the bottom edge along the bottom row to the opposite side, making a Z/S path corner to corner.

slots.vertical: marker column, full height, except the marker
slots.top turn: along row 0 to the left edge in pairs 0,2 and to the right edge in pair 1
slots.bottom turn: along last row to the opposite edge
slots.side rule: unclear: pair 1 (5x5, marker at exact centre (2,2)) turns right at top; pairs 0 (8x8,(3,2)) and 2 (7x7,(3,4)) turn left at top

why: output = input plus a 1-cell-wide colour-1 path through the marker column joining opposite grid corners

reading: Each loose object (not the floor colour that fills the bottom) drops straight down as a rigid piece until it is one cell above the floor colour (or the bottom edge); a piece landing on an already dropped piece stacks directly on it.

slots.subjects: objects of colours other than bg 7 and the floor colour (bottom-row colour)
slots.stop: leave exactly one bg cell above the floor colour / bottom edge; stack flush on previously dropped pieces (process lowest first)

why: each piece keeps its shape and column; it ends with a one-cell gap above the floor (not in contact, so move/obstacle does not fit)

reading: One row is a full pattern; every other non-empty row shows only a prefix. Each partial row is completed by copying the full row's pattern with colours renamed by the correspondence its prefix gives (full-row colour at a column -> partial-row colour there).

slots.targets: rows with a non-bg prefix and bg tail
slots.key: per row: exemplar colour -> target colour read from the prefix columns
slots.action: write key(exemplar[x]) into every column of the target row

why: each target row equals the exemplar row recoloured by its own prefix-derived map

reading: The single marker moves down one cell; every row above its new position is filled with colour 4 in the columns of the same parity as the marker's column.

slots.subject: the one marker
slots.stripe: rows 0..original marker row, columns x with x = marker column (mod 2), colour 4

why: marker at (r+1,c); cells (y<=r, x%2==c%2) are 4; all else bg

reading: The input holds several boxes; a smaller piece fits exactly into a hole-pattern of a larger box (pieces nest into matching holes). The output is the largest box with the other pieces inserted into their matching holes.

slots.pieces: smaller boxes whose shape/colour fits a hole pattern inside a bigger box
slots.placement: each piece replaces the matching hole region of the box it fits, recursively

why: output is the container box with all pieces nested into their matching holes

reading: A bracket frame (four 4 corners with two coloured side bars) is cut out, and the two-coloured shape is placed between the bars, mirrored left-right if needed so each colour sits next to the bar of the same colour.

slots.frame: the 4-cornered bracket with two vertical bars (output box)
slots.orientation: identity or horizontal flip so its left colour equals the left bar colour
slots.placement: piece fills the interior between the bars

why: output = bracket box with the piece (possibly flipped) filling its interior
invariants: piece shape up to horizontal flip

reading: Each closed outline has a hole of one or two cells; one-cell holes are filled with 5 and two-cell holes with 7.

new_rows.name: hole1
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
inner(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0, Ya = Y - 1, Yb = Y + 1, Xa = X - 1, Xb = X + 1, px(Ya, X, A), px(Yb, X, B), px(Y, Xa, D), px(Y, Xb, E).
bgnb(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- inner(Y, X), orth(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C), C = 0.
hasbg(Y, X) :- bgnb(Y, X, N).
hole1(Y, X) :- inner(Y, X), !hasbg(Y, X).

new_rows.name: hole2
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
inner(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0, Ya = Y - 1, Yb = Y + 1, Xa = X - 1, Xb = X + 1, px(Ya, X, A), px(Yb, X, B), px(Y, Xa, D), px(Y, Xb, E).
bgnb(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- inner(Y, X), orth(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C), C = 0.
one(Y, X) :- bgnb(Y, X, N), N = 1.
hole2(Y, X) :- one(Y, X), orth(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, one(Y2, X2).

why: 1-cell enclosed bg cells become 5 (stage 1), 2-cell enclosed bg pairs become 7 (stage 2); nothing else changes

reading: A 5 separator splits the grid into two panels, each with a colour-2 bar and a colour-4 bar. The output is a 2x2 block of whichever colour's bar grew more from the top panel to the bottom panel.

slots.panels: top and bottom halves cut by the 5 row
slots.measure: per colour: bottom-panel bar length minus top-panel bar length
slots.output: 2x2 filled with the colour of larger growth

why: growth (2 vs 4): pair0 3>2, pair1 3>2, pair2 2>1 -> 2; pair3 1<2 -> 4

reading: Each 2x2 block of 2 has four coloured cells at its diagonal corners; those corner colours rotate one step clockwise around the block, and from each corner a diagonal ray in its new colour runs outward to the grid edge.

slots.unit: each 2x2 block of colour 2 with its 4 diagonal corner cells
slots.recolour: new TL=old BL, TR=old TL, BR=old TR, BL=old BR
slots.rays: from each corner, diagonal away from the block to the border in the corner's new colour; where rays cross, later/other rays may overwrite

why: blocks unchanged; corner colours are a clockwise rotation; diagonal rays carry those colours to the edge
